tasks.title: Derive wall paint area from perimeter × height
tasks.notes: Deduct door/window openings from gross wall area

prep.what: Implement the formula that computes paintable wall area per room: (perimeter × ceiling height) minus door and window opening areas.
prep.understand: Paint area is the gross wall surface minus any openings. This drives the paint material line item in the estimate — getting this right means the cost auto-calculates from the blueprint dimensions rather than manual entry.
approach: Find the room measurement model (perimeter, ceiling height, openings list) — this is where drywall area is likely already computed; paint area follows the same shape.
Implement `compute_paint_area(room)` → gross = perimeter × height, net = gross − sum(opening areas).
Write a unit test: hardcode one room's dimensions and verify the expected paint area comes out.
Plug `compute_paint_area` into the assembly pricing pipeline so it feeds the paint line item.
resources: Takeoff engine room/polygon measurement model (look for `perimeter`, `ceiling_height`, `openings` fields)
Existing drywall-area formula (parallel pattern — same inputs, different deduction set)
Assembly pricing pipeline entry point
Unit test suite for assembly computations

tasks.title: Route takeoff measurements to trades at seam
tasks.notes: The seam is the interface between raw measurement engine and estimate builder

prep.what: Wire takeoff engine output (room measurements) to the trade routing layer so each measurement auto-assigns to the correct trade category (paint, drywall, flooring, etc.) before entering the estimate.
prep.understand: The 'seam' is the handoff point between the blueprint parser/measurement engine and the estimate builder. Right now measurements probably flow through as raw numbers. Trade routing tags each measurement with its trade so the estimate builder knows which QB item category to price it under.
approach: List the measurement types the engine outputs (wall area, floor area, ceiling area, fixture count, linear ft) and map each to a trade code.
Implement `route_to_trade(measurement_type) → trade_code` — a lookup table is fine for v1.
Insert the routing step into the pipeline between raw measurement output and assembly pricing input.
Smoke-test with one sample plan: confirm wall area → paint + drywall, floor area → flooring, etc.
resources: AZ Takeoff assembly/trade schema (how QB items are categorized by trade)

tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room: paint, drywall, flooring + wall heights
tasks.notes: Already in-progress — pick up from current state and close it today

prep.what: Build the assemblies-per-room data pipeline: for each room, derive the area quantities (paint, drywall, flooring) from wall perimeter × ceiling height and floor polygon area, then link these to the assembly line items.
prep.understand: Assemblies are material categories — paint covers walls + ceiling, drywall covers walls only, flooring covers the floor polygon. Each room's assembly quantities feed directly into the estimate line items. Wall heights must come from the blueprint dimension annotations, not defaults.
approach: Review your in-progress branch: understand what's already wired and what's missing to close this task.
Confirm wall height extraction is working (from dimension annotations on the blueprint) for at least 2-3 test rooms.
For each assembly type, verify the area formula: paint = walls (perimeter × height) + ceiling area; drywall = walls only; flooring = floor polygon area.
Run the pipeline on a full test plan and verify per-room assembly quantities in the output; fix any rooms with missing or zero heights.

tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text + callout filtering
tasks.notes: Outlined/stroke-only text requires a different detection path than filled text

prep.what: Upgrade the label detection lane to handle outlined (stroke-only) text using M3 vision, and add a filter to exclude callout bubbles from being classified as measurement labels.
prep.understand: Construction plans use two text styles: solid-fill text (already handled by lane v1) and outlined/stroked text where only the glyph outline is drawn, no fill. Callout bubbles are balloon-style annotation markers — they surround notes or specs, not measurements — and must not feed the label classifier.
approach: Profile the current lane v1: find where it misclassifies outlined text and what false positives callout bubbles create.
Add a preprocessing step for outlined-text detection — try contour analysis (no fill interior) or a dedicated M3 vision model call with a 'outlined text' prompt.
Implement a callout-bubble filter: detect circular/speech-bubble contour shapes and exclude them from label output before classification.
Validate on 2-3 test sheets with known outlined text and callouts — measure precision/recall delta vs. lane v1.
resources: M3 vision API (structured output mode for text region classification)
Label lane v1 pipeline code (current detection + classification entry points)
Sample plan sheets with outlined annotations and callout bubbles (use sheets from the test fixture set)
OpenCV contour analysis utilities (already in repo if drywall detection uses them)
